title: Degree of the canonical bundle
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve of dimension one over $k$ [def-sc-curves], of genus $g=\dim_k H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-sc-genus]. Put $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ [def-sc-kahler-differentials]. There is a divisor $K_C$ on $C$ [def-sc-divisor] such that $\omega_C\cong\mathcal O_C(K_C)$ and $\deg K_C=2g-2$. In fact, every divisor $K$ with $\mathcal O_C(K)\cong\omega_C$ has degree $2g-2$, with degree as in [def-sc-pic0].

proof.text: The canonical sheaf $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is invertible by [lem-sc-canonical-sheaf]. The curve is integral by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Apply [lem-sc-line-bundle-rational-section] to $\omega_C$: a nonzero rational section $s$ gives the divisor $K_C=\operatorname{div}(s)$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C(K_C)\cong\omega_C$.

source.place: canonical bundle clause, supplemented by the divisor realization in unit sk-thm-picard-rr, Degrees

proof.text: For the structure sheaf, [lem-sc-global-functions] gives $h^0(\mathcal O_C)=1$ and [def-sc-genus] gives $h^1(\mathcal O_C)=g$. For $\omega_C$, apply [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] with $\mathcal M=\mathcal O_C$: the two dualities in dimensions zero and one give $h^0(\omega_C)=h^1(\mathcal O_C)=g$ and $h^1(\omega_C)=h^0(\mathcal O_C)=1$. Vanishing above dimension one from [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] makes the Euler characteristics $\chi(\mathcal O_C)=1-g$ and $\chi(\omega_C)=g-1$.

source.place: Step (RR), computation of the degree of the canonical sheaf by duality

proof.text: Apply the line-bundle clause of [lem-sc-riemann-roch] to the invertible $\omega_C$ of Step 1: $\chi(\omega_C)=\deg\omega_C+1-g$. Substituting the value $g-1$ from Step 2 gives $\deg\omega_C=2g-2$, the degree identity for the dualizing sheaf on this smooth connected curve.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0BS6, parts (1) and (2), via unit sk-thm-picard-rr Step (RR)

proof.text: By the degree definition [def-sc-pic0], any $K$ satisfying $\mathcal O_C(K)\cong\omega_C$ has $\deg K=\deg\omega_C$. In particular the divisor $K_C$ constructed in Step 1 has degree $2g-2$ by Step 3.

source.place: Degrees, divisor and line-bundle degree agree
